title: Lean protocol: seven untied transformer blocks instead of six (5.58M params) on the 101-claude Lean incumbent
description: P24/P25-family depth axis (not P01: all seven blocks untied): N_LAYER 6 -> 7 at d_model 256, the only edit to 101-claude's pretrain.py, testing whether the one Lean-protocol result so far (5 -> 6 blocks: +16, every seed up, after the same step lost -12 under the token format) is a trend or a noise draw. If Lean's longer have-chains with scoped n_k names reward sequential composition depth, a seventh block should give expert iteration more correct long proofs to bootstrap from, at the cost of ~14% fewer pretraining steps and ~15% slower sampling that the 2400 s cap should absorb (101 totals 1848-1926 s).
hypothesis: Depth bounds how many attention hops the model composes per token; each Lean step must resolve which n_k names are in scope and which earlier facts justify the next have, and 101's gain came from more correct long proofs (eval parse failures fell ~7%, round-1 unbound-name failures did not fall), i.e. better multi-step composition. If the 6-block model is still depth-limited on L>=7 proofs, a seventh block raises round-4 targets solved and dev >=7 solves; pretraining val loss already plateaus well before 300 s, so ~3,100 steps (~2.6 epochs, vs 3,607 and 3.0) should cost little fit. If 101's +16 was a noise draw (3-seed-mean sd ~25) or pretraining is now step-limited, this reads flat or negative.
expected_delta: -35 to +40 dev solves >= 7 (central +5); pretraining ~3,000-3,150 steps vs 3,573-3,624 (~2.5-2.6 epochs), final val loss 0.078-0.085, RL sampling ~160-195 samples/s vs 184-220, totals ~2,000-2,250 s (no timeout expected; a slow pod is the main risk)

arch.change: CHANGED vs 101-claude: N_LAYER 6 -> 7 (one more untied block); everything else identical
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 7, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=7 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.6
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (7 per sample), unchanged fork code

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: unchanged from 078-claude: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2, head (107,256) 1.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 28 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 7 blocks) plus head.weight (107,256; vocab 107, no bias) are in Muon: 29 matrices. Seven qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (107<256) so it is not transposed.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: unchanged from 081-claude: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2).

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 29 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Same rule as 101-claude with seven blocks: fork default construction, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. The extra block's init draws shift the global RNG stream relative to 101-claude.
